answers.text: Welke stap heeft nu de meeste waarde?
answers.english: Which step has the most value now?
answers.explanation: Question word and inversion. Welke stap is itself the question subject and is followed by finite heeft; no extra subject is inserted. A question word/phrase comes first, then the finite verb and subject. In a subject question the question phrase itself is the subject, so no extra subject is needed. Welke stap is the singular question subject of heeft. De meeste waarde asks which step is most useful now, not which has already succeeded.

Ik ben bezig met het onderzoek naar de v.scenario: You are explaining the next diagnostic step to a colleague, setting an observation or review point without promising success. Describe your ongoing investigation.

answers.text: Ik ben bezig met het onderzoek naar de vertraging.
answers.english: I am investigating the delay.
answers.explanation: Bezig with an activity. The first constituent is Ik; ben is the finite (conjugated) verb and Ik is its subject. In a declarative main clause, the finite verb is second in constituents, not necessarily second in individual words. A finite form of zijn plus bezig describes an ongoing activity. Met takes an activity noun/nominalised infinitive; a te-infinitive construction names the action directly. Do not confuse met with the conjunction terwijl. Ben bezig met describes ongoing work. Het onderzoek is a noun after met and naar de vertraging identifies its topic; onderzoeken is not the written form used in this model.

Als deze test niets oplevert, vragen we.scenario: You are explaining the next diagnostic step to a colleague, setting an observation or review point without promising success. Explain the fallback if testing is inconclusive.

answers.text: Als deze test niets oplevert, vragen we extra hulp.
answers.english: If this test yields nothing, we will ask for extra help.
answers.explanation: Fronted subordinate clause. The first constituent is Als deze test niets oplevert,; vragen is the finite (conjugated) verb and we is its subject. In a declarative main clause, the finite verb is second in constituents, not necessarily second in individual words. The complete subordinate clause counts as the first constituent of the main clause. The main finite verb follows it, then the main subject. Inside the subordinate clause its own verb/group comes toward the end. The als-clause ends in oplevert. Niets is its object, meaning no useful result here; main vragen we follows with extra hulp as the fallback request.
